_meta.purpose: Curated SSOT for /rrm-success-rates/ evidence pillar. Every statistic on the page, in charts, and in chart alt text derives from this file.
_meta.verification_rule: No row renders on the page unless verified:true with a verificationNote naming the exact source location. Rows with excluded:true never render.
_meta.outcome_type_rule: Never blend conception rates into live-birth comparisons. outcomeType drives table grouping and chart eligibility.

studies.authors: Stanford JB, Parnell TA, Boyle PC
studies.journal: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine
studies.population: avg age 35.8; 33% prior ART; 5.6 yr trying
studies.notes: Crude 25.5% vs adjusted (life-table) cumulative 52.8% @24mo (label both explicitly). adjCumConception 0.648 = adjusted-cumulative ANY conception 64.8% @24mo (Table 3). Crude is the conservative measure (dropouts treated as continuing, ITT-like); adjusted = life-table censoring withdrawals (not strict per-protocol vs ITT, but functions analogously). Twins 4.6% among live births.
studies.verificationNote: Fulltext Tables 3-4 + abstract: crude LBR 25.5%/100 @24mo (19.1% @12mo), adjusted life-table 52.8% @24mo (27.1% @12mo); adjusted-cumulative any-conception 64.8% @24mo (Table 3); n=1072, avg age 35.8, 33% prior ART, 5.6 yr trying, twins 4.6% (13 of 273 live births). DOI+PMID from library record, both PubMed-verified (PMID 18772291, J Am Board Fam Med 2008).

studies.notes: Recurrent-miscarriage subgroup: 19/108 (18%) had 2+ prior unexplained miscarriages. All births singleton. CORRECTION: crudeLbr filled to 0.38 from abstract (was seeded null).
studies.verificationNote: Abstract (Results): adjusted cumulative first-live-birth 66/100 @24mo, crude 38%; adjusted cumulative first-conception 73/100, crude 47%; n=108, avg age 35.4, mean 3.2 yr trying, 8% (9/108) prior ART, 22% (24/108) prior IUI; all singleton, 54% at 37+ wks. CRUDE-vs-ADJCUM CLASSIFICATION (fulltext-verified 2026-06-03): adjCumConception 0.73 is GENUINELY adjusted-cumulative -- Table 4 reports first-conception 'Adjusted proportion† 73.1' at 24mo, with footnote '†Adjusted by life-table analysis, where withdrawal or continuing treatment at the end of study follow-up are censoring events'; the crude proportion (47.2%) is reported as a separate column. So 0.73 STAYS in adjCumConception, NOT crudeConception.

studies.authors: Boyle P, Toth A, Minjeur M, Turczynski C
studies.population: mean age 36.4; 19% prior IVF (2.3 cycles); mean 32.2 mo trying; 2019 Dublin clinic cohort
studies.notes: First head-to-head RRM vs IVF (benchmarked vs CDC/SART/HFEA 2019). CORRECTIONS: (1) mean age 36.4 NOT 33.6 (seeded age was wrong); (2) adjCumConception 0.52 is the CRUDE conception rate 52% (98/187), NOT adjusted-cumulative (paper reports crude only). Prematurity (apples-to-apples): RRM singleton 4.0% (3/75) vs CDC singleton 11.8%; RRM all-pregnancy 6.5% vs SART all-pregnancy 14.4%. Funnel 249 consults -> 187 treated -> 98 conceived -> 77 live births. crudeLbr 0.41 = 77/187 = 41.2% (paper states 41%). Diagnostic reassignment: unexplained 24%->1%, corpus luteum deficiency 0%->71%.
studies.verificationNote: Abstract + body (Results): 249 had >=1 consult, 187 met inclusion; 52% (98/187) crude conception, 41% (77/187) crude LBR (paper states 41%; 77/187=41.2%); 75 singletons + 2 twin sets = 79 babies; mean age 36.4, mean 32.2 mo trying, 19% (35/187) prior IVF. Singleton prematurity 4.0% (3/75, 33-37wk) vs CDC singleton 11.8%; all-pregnancy 6.5% RRM vs SART 14.4%; LBW 5.3% (4/75). Age-band head-to-head (body): 42.0% RRM vs 40% SART (<43yr, multi-transfer), 44.0% RRM vs 41% CDC (<41yr). DOI from library record (JRRM not PubMed-indexed, so pmid stays null); JRRM is a specialty (non-MEDLINE) journal -- journalTier 'specialty' retained.

studies.authors: Sánchez-Méndez JI, Lombarte M, Abengózar-Muela R, et al.
studies.population: mean age 35.0; 27.5% prior ART; median 24 mo infertility; Madrid (Fertilitas Center) single center, 5-year cohort
studies.notes: Largest NaPro cohort to date (take-home-baby). adjCumLbr 0.50 = adjusted cumulative 50.0% @22-24mo (Table 3); plateau 62.1% reached at the 31-33mo band and unchanged through the 34-36mo band. CORRECTION: author surname is Sánchez-Méndez JI (first name José Ignacio), not '-Méndez S'. Cumulative-over-time, by-age, by-diagnosis chart data extracted in verification pass.
studies.verificationNote: Abstract + Table 3 + Fig 2B: crude take-home-baby (live birth) 35.3% (463/1310); adjusted cumulative THB 62.1% overall (95% CI 58.8-65.4), with Table 3 time-curve giving 50.0% @22-24mo (CI 48.1-51.9) and 62.1% plateau @31-33mo; by age (Fig 2B, adjusted cumulative) 83.7% (18-30), 63.2% (31-35), 53.3% (36-40), 24.4% (>40); mean age 35.0, 27.5% (360/1310) prior ART (crude THB 25.3% in that subgroup). DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 41323405, Front Reprod Health, 14 Nov 2025). Table 3 cells cross-checked on live Frontiers page.

studies.authors: Barbato M, Del Zoppo S, Parazzini F, Graziani A, Guida M, Ferlin A, Frigerio L, Grande G
studies.population: FAM arm n=41 of 97 total (41 FAM vs 56 ART control); primary idiopathic infertility, female age <40, seeking natural conception; CAMeN symptothermal method; multicenter Italy 2010-2014
studies.notes: n CORRECTED: seed n=97 was the TOTAL (41 FAM + 56 ART); the RRM/FAM arm is n=41. adjCumConception 0.5122 = crude FAM-arm pregnancy rate 51.22% (21/41 spontaneous pregnancies) at 12mo (cumulative proportion calculated at 12mo per the paper's Statistical Analysis). FAM age<34 subgroup 90.9% (10/11); age 35-39 36.7% (11/30). ART control arm: 17.8% (10/56) per complete ART cycle (NOT a 12mo cumulative -- different denominator, do not plot head-to-head as if same metric). FAM pregnancies obtained after 5.9 +/- 3.9 months. This is FAM/symptothermal waiting-conduct, not full NaPro medical/surgical RRM.
studies.verificationNote: Fulltext abstract + Results: FAM group n=41 (of a 97-couple total study, 56 in the ART comparator arm); 21 spontaneous pregnancies = pregnancy rate 51.22%; age<34 (n=11) 90.9% (10/11); age 35-39 (n=30) 36.7% (11/30); ART arm 17.8% (10/56) per complete cycle; FAM conceptions at 5.9+/-3.9 mo; cumulative proportions calculated at 12mo (Statistical Analysis). Multicenter Italy 2010-2014, CAMeN symptothermal method, idiopathic infertility (female age <40, BMI<25). DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 41883420, Front Reprod Health 2026; esummary title/journal/authors match).

studies.authors: Bernot G, Lallemand L, Le Menager C, Ecochard R
studies.journal: European Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology and Reproductive Biology
studies.population: French couples receiving fertility counselling + treatment 2022-2023 via trained fertility instructors + 15 GPs with fertility-chart-based therapeutic patient education; 4 of 551 women lost to follow-up (547 analyzed)
studies.notes: MATCH CONFIRMED (not a wrong record): this GP/therapeutic-patient-education paper IS the source of n=551. CORRECTIONS: (1) adjCumConception 0.37 is the CRUDE conception proportion 37% (204/547), NOT actuarial/life-table -- the abstract reports a crude rate only. (2) DROPPED the seed's 'actuarial ~40-60% at 1yr' claim: NOT present in this paper (do not assert). (3) DROPPED the seed's '2 yr average trying' population claim: NOT stated in the abstract. Of the 204 who conceived, 75% had a live birth or ongoing pregnancy at study cut-off (so a derived crude LBR/ongoing is ~28% (153/547), but the paper frames the 75% as proportion-of-conceivers, not a cumulative LBR -- left out of crudeLbr to avoid a manufactured endpoint). Fertility-chart-mediated RRM-adjacent model (GPs + instructors), not a NaPro medical-protocol cohort.
studies.verificationNote: Abstract (Results): of 551 women, only 4 lost to follow-up; of the remaining 547, 204 (37%) became pregnant; of these, 75% had a live birth or ongoing pregnancy at study cut-off. 66 French fertility instructors + 15 trained GPs interviewed June 2024; records of couples counselled/treated 1 Jan 2022-31 Dec 2023. No actuarial/1yr figure and no '2yr trying' figure in the paper -- both seed claims dropped. DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 40209491, Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol 2025 Jun; esummary title/journal/authors match exactly). MATCH VERIFIED -- this is the correct n=551 record, no wrong-match.

studies.authors: Grande G, Garolla A, Graziani A, Astorri AL, Cammarota MV, Merola A, Polidori MP, Lulli E, Busato E, Pesce F, Pompa G, Pontecorvi A, Milardi D, Ferlin A
studies.population: 1,014 couples with primary infertility, comprehensive male-factor (andrological) + gynecological workup; male mean age 37.7, female 33.4; 266/1014 (26%) prior ART failure; 919 treated after excluding 95 untreatable causes; multicenter Italy 2015-2022
studies.notes: Male-factor workup cohort. adjCumConception 0.409 = crude spontaneous pregnancy rate 40.9% (376/919) among treated couples after targeted etiologic treatment (NOT life-table adjusted). CORRECTIONS: (1) prior-ART-failure 26% (266/1014) NOT 28.9% (seed value wrong); (2) followUpMonths set to 12 (minimum follow-up 12mo per fulltext). Idiopathic infertility reduced from typical 30-50% to 8% (82/1014) after full workup. Isolated male factor 23%; combined 45%. Isolated male-factor subgroup spontaneous pregnancy 32.5% (68/209 treated). RRM-structured: fertility-awareness practitioner embedded in the diagnostic team, ART explicitly refused by participants, etiologic correction philosophy. No control arm vs immediate ART.
studies.verificationNote: Abstract + fulltext body: n=1,014 couples (266=26% prior ART failure); isolated male factor 23%, combined 45%, idiopathic reduced to 8% (82/1014); 95 untreatable excluded -> 919 treated; targeted treatment -> spontaneous pregnancy 40.9% (376/919). By female age: <34 53.73%, 35-39 34.30%, 40-42 14.78%, >43 3.83%. Isolated male-factor subgroup 32.5% (68/209). Min follow-up 12mo, multicenter Italy 2015-2022 (incl. Paul VI ISI natural reproductive medicine centre, Gemelli IRCCS). DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 39930939, Andrology 2025 Nov, 13(8):2122-2130; esummary title/journal/authors match).

studies.verificationNote: Abstract (Main Results): among all couples 57% had at least one pregnancy and 44% at least one live birth during follow-up (crude, clinic/participant-reported); n=834 subfertile couples, 10 sites in 4 countries (USA/Canada/UK/Poland), mean woman age 34.0, 30% (199/659) prior live birth, mean 4.7 diagnoses/couple. studies.authors: Marshell M, Corkill M, Whitty M, Thomas A, Turner J

studies.authors: Frank-Herrmann P, Jacobs C, Jenetzky E, Gnoth C, Pyper C, Baur S, Freundl G, Goeckenjan M, Strowitzki T
studies.population: 187 subfertile women trained in the Sensiplan symptothermal method; age 21-47; mean 3.5 yr trying (range 1-8); amenorrhea, known tubal occlusion and severe male factor excluded
studies.notes: adjCumConception 0.38 = cumulative pregnancy rate 38% (95% CI 27-49%; 58 pregnancies) after 8 observation months -- life-table cumulative, all-comers. Subgroup trying 1-2 yr: 56% @8mo. Reference comparator: estimated basic pregnancy rate 21.6% in untrained couples from the same cohort (7 women conceived in the cycle immediately prior to training). Unfavorable: female age >35 (cum PR 25%, p=0.06); trying >2yr (cum PR 17%, p<0.01). Fertility-awareness training only (Sensiplan), not a NaPro medical/surgical RRM cohort. crudeLbr null -- conception (not live-birth) endpoint.
studies.verificationNote: Abstract (Results): cumulative pregnancy rate 38% (95% CI 27-49%, 58 pregnancies) after 8 months Sensiplan training, vs estimated 21.6% basic rate in untrained couples same cohort; 1-2yr-trying subgroup 56% @8mo; age>35 25% (p=0.06); >2yr 17% (p<0.01). n=187 subfertile women, age 21-47, mean 3.5yr trying (range 1-8). DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 28185073, Arch Gynecol Obstet 2017 Apr, 295(4):1015-1024; esummary title/journal/authors match). CRUDE-vs-ADJCUM CLASSIFICATION (fulltext-verified 2026-06-03): adjCumConception 0.38 is GENUINELY cumulative -- the paper's stated Purpose is 'To analyze cumulative pregnancy rates' and Results report 'The cumulative pregnancy rate ... was 38% (95% CI 27-49%; 58 pregnancies) after eight observation months'; subgroup figures (1-2yr 56%, age>35 25%, >2yr 17%) are all framed as 'cumulative pregnancy rate' over the 8mo observation window. So 0.38 STAYS in adjCumConception, NOT crudeConception (label rendered as 'adj. cum. conception 38% @8mo').

safety_comparators.authors: Simonsen SE, Baksh L, Stanford JB
safety_comparators.finding: ART singletons: preterm OR 3.28 (95% CI 1.74-6.20), low birthweight OR 2.91 (1.99-4.26) vs never-treated referent; n=21,803 surveyed, weighted to 1,022,597. Year resolved to print 2016 (epub 2015-07-07).
safety_comparators.verificationNote: Abstract (Results, referent group 1, singletons): ART preterm OR 3.28 (CI 1.74-6.20), LBW OR 2.91 (CI 1.99-4.26); n=21,803 weighted to 1,022,597; FL/MD/UT 2004-2008. YEAR RECONCILED: PubMed esummary gives print pubdate 2016 Apr (BJOG vol 123, issue 5, pp 718-29), epub 2015 Jul 7 -> year set to citable print 2016. DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 26148540).
safety_comparators.humanReadable: For single babies, the adjusted odds of being born early were about 3 times higher after ART, and the odds of low birth weight about 3 times higher, compared with women who never used fertility treatment. These are adjusted odds, not a head-count percentage; the study did not publish a single-baby percentage for each group, so we keep the 'times higher' wording.

absoluteRates.scope: all births per group, crude/unadjusted (Table 2, weighted %); NOT the singleton-adjusted figures behind OR 3.28 / 2.91
absoluteRates.context_note: Crude all-births rates are heavily driven by multiple gestation (ART multiple-gestation rate 33.2% vs 1.2% in never-treated, Table 2). Do NOT pair these crude all-births rates with the singleton-restricted, covariate-adjusted OR 3.28/2.91 as if they were the same comparison.
absoluteRates.verificationNote: Simonsen 2016 Table 2 (PDF body, 'Adverse pregnancy outcomes among PRAMS respondents'): preterm delivery <37wk ART 30.9% (95% CI 23.3-38.5) vs no-treatment 10.1% (9.2-11.0); low birthweight <2500g ART 26.7% (21.5-31.9) vs 6.1% (5.9-6.3); multiple gestation ART 33.2% vs 1.2%. These are all-births weighted %, not singleton-only. Tables 3-4 (singleton-specific) report ORs only, no per-group absolute singleton rate.

safety_comparators.authors: Sanders JN, Simonsen SE, Porucznik CA, Hammoud AO, Smith KR, Stanford JB
safety_comparators.finding: Adjusted preterm-birth odds vs untreated subfertile women: IVF OR 4.24 (95% CI 2.05-8.77); IUI OR 3.17 (1.40-7.19); ovulation drugs OR 2.17 (0.99-4.75). Linked-data retrospective cohort, 487 first births.
safety_comparators.verificationNote: Abstract (Results): adjusted ORs for preterm birth vs untreated subfertile women -- IVF 4.24 (CI 2.05-8.77), IUI 3.17 (CI 1.40-7.19), ovulation drugs 2.17 (CI 0.99-4.75); 487 first-birth certificates + 3 fetal deaths linked, 19% PTB overall; Univ of Utah FES 2010-2012. DOI+PMID from library record, PubMed-verified (PMID 35351163, Reprod Health 2022).
safety_comparators.humanReadable: Among women who were already struggling with subfertility, the adjusted odds of an early (preterm) birth were about 4 times higher after IVF and about 3 times higher after IUI, compared with subfertile women who used no treatment that cycle. These are adjusted odds, not a head-count percentage; the study reports an overall preterm rate of 19% but does not publish a separate preterm percentage for each treatment group, so we keep the 'times higher' wording.

absoluteRates.note: Sanders 2022 reports preterm odds ratios by treatment (Table 4) but NO per-treatment absolute preterm percentage. Only overall PTB (19%) and singleton PTB (9.2%, 38/412 in Table 1) are absolute. Treatment-group Ns exist (Table 2: none 213, drugs 77, IUI 64, IVF 136) but without per-group event counts, a true relative risk cannot be computed. Stays odds-ratio framing.
absoluteRates.verificationNote: Sanders 2022 PDF body: Table 4 = unadjusted/adjusted ORs by most-invasive treatment (IVF adj OR 4.24, IUI 3.17, drugs 2.17). Table 1 = PTB by demographics (singleton PTB 9.2%). Table 3 = PTB by diagnosis. No table reports PTB% by treatment type. Abstract: 'Among linked births, 19% had a PTB.'

safety_comparators_chart.metric: perinatal safety comparators (preterm / LBW / multiples) for the grouped safety chart
safety_comparators_chart._note: Mixed metrics across studies; grouping must keep singleton-vs-all-pregnancy and rate-vs-OR distinctions explicit (do NOT plot a 4.0% rate on the same axis as a 3.28 OR). Only paper-sourced values included; nothing approximated.

preterm_rates_singleton.label: RRM singleton preterm (Boyle 2025)
preterm_rates_singleton.humanReadable: About 4 in 100 single babies were born early after RRM, versus about 12 in 100 in the CDC IVF benchmark -- roughly two-thirds fewer (4.0% vs 11.8%).
preterm_rates_singleton.humanReadableNote: Relative reduction computed from the two absolute rates: 1 - (4.0/11.8) = 66%. True relative-risk style statement, NOT an odds-ratio conversion.
preterm_rates_singleton.verificationNote: Boyle 2025 abstract: 4.0% (3/75) of singleton babies preterm (33-37 wk)

preterm_rates_singleton.label: CDC IVF singleton preterm benchmark
preterm_rates_singleton.humanReadable: About 12 in 100 single IVF babies were born early (CDC benchmark).
preterm_rates_singleton.verificationNote: Boyle 2025 abstract: '11.8% CDC, singleton pregnancies' benchmark

preterm_rates_all_pregnancies.label: RRM all-pregnancy preterm (Boyle 2025)
preterm_rates_all_pregnancies.humanReadable: Across all RRM pregnancies, about 7 in 100 babies were born early, versus about 14 in 100 in the SART IVF benchmark -- more than half fewer (6.5% vs 14.4%).
preterm_rates_all_pregnancies.humanReadableNote: Relative reduction computed from the two absolute rates: 1 - (6.5/14.4) = 55%. True relative-risk style statement, NOT an odds-ratio conversion.

preterm_rates_all_pregnancies.label: SART IVF all-pregnancy preterm benchmark
preterm_rates_all_pregnancies.humanReadable: Across all IVF pregnancies, about 14 in 100 babies were born early (SART benchmark).

multiples_rate.label: RRM twins (Boyle 2018, post-IVF cohort)
multiples_rate.humanReadable: Only about 1 in 70 RRM births was a twin pregnancy (1.4%) -- RRM transfers one naturally-conceived embryo at a time, so multiples are rare.
multiples_rate.verificationNote: Boyle 2018: only one twin pregnancy / 74 live births = 1.4%

preterm_odds_ratios.label: ART singleton preterm OR (Simonsen 2016)
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadable: Adjusted odds of early birth about 3 times higher for single babies after ART, versus women who never used fertility treatment.
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadableNote: Adjusted odds ratio, singleton-restricted. No matching per-group singleton percentage published, so kept as 'times higher (adjusted odds)' -- NOT converted to a percent.
preterm_odds_ratios.verificationNote: Simonsen 2016 abstract, referent 1, singletons: ART preterm OR 3.28 (1.74-6.20)

preterm_odds_ratios.label: IVF preterm OR (Sanders 2022)
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadable: Adjusted odds of early birth about 4 times higher after IVF, versus subfertile women who used no treatment that cycle.
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadableNote: Adjusted odds ratio. No per-treatment preterm percentage published, so kept as 'times higher (adjusted odds)' -- NOT converted to a percent.

preterm_odds_ratios.label: IUI preterm OR (Sanders 2022)
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadable: Adjusted odds of early birth about 3 times higher after IUI, versus subfertile women who used no treatment that cycle.
preterm_odds_ratios.humanReadableNote: Adjusted odds ratio. No per-treatment preterm percentage published, so kept as 'times higher (adjusted odds)' -- NOT converted to a percent.

lbw_odds_ratios.label: ART singleton LBW OR (Simonsen 2016)
lbw_odds_ratios.humanReadable: Adjusted odds of low birth weight about 3 times higher for single babies after ART, versus women who never used fertility treatment.
